analysis:
The supplied change is documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md). The base text units are the Qwen TP, media ingress and cluster runtime-facts sections. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the visible head-side changes are: a date bump; a paragraph on the cluster-service heartbeat file (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json vs part-health.json, PID-matched liveness guard); and a rewrite of the 'Cluster runtime facts' intro. The rewrite says a signed release computes approval digests from its own final app and registers them as `cluster_runtime`, and that guided setup matches a served approval using the same computation. No code, wire format, key handling or authorization logic changes in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant points for integration: (1) The runtime-facts text touches the TB-009/TB-011 trust-contract area (installed-file digests, capability digest, resource policy digest). It describes release-lane registration of digests, but the registration endpoint, who authorizes it and the release-lane implementation are outside the supplied evidence. If that registration is a new API, its authentication belongs under A-005 / A-011 and the threat model may need updating. This cannot be judged from the docs alone. (2) The heartbeat-file separation text says the supervisor's liveness guard accepts only a beat with the service's own PID. That is a local same-UID availability concern in the style of T-060 or T-043, but it is documentation only here, and the underlying code is not supplied. (3) The base-side Qwen sections (media admission, prefix tenant partitions, encrypted SSD prefix cache) are unchanged by this PR, so I raised no pre-existing T-041 or SEC-035 concerns. I did not verify the truncated patch remainder. No concrete regressions or new attack surface are evidenced.
